judgments.lesson: The quoted-spread state does not identify tradeable liquidity concessions on USDJPY at the intraday horizon, and the liquidity-provision family (conditioning on clock, level, size, tick volume and now spread) is closed. The hypothesis cell (one-hour move >= 0.25 x ATR20 with the M15 spread proxy >= 2 x its same-slot median, scheduled releases and the rollover excluded, two-hour time exit) had 160 design episodes on 123 trading days and made -0.020 R net (t -0.31; clustered t +0.22) with a gross of exactly 0.000 R on bid/ask fills, so the concession is competed away before a market order fills; the one-bar delay arm made -0.058 R (t -0.94); check was -0.065 and -0.081 R; the 0.40 x ATR cells -0.078 and -0.107 R. The no-spread-condition control measured the plain one-hour intraday shock fade on USDJPY for the first time at scale: -0.068 R (t -4.5, 2075 trades, every design year negative, gross -0.039 R before commission) and -0.073 R in check (t -4.2, 1629 trades); news-inclusive -0.070 R on 3576 trades. So one-hour moves of a quarter ATR keep going for the next two hours, by about 2 percent of the move on mid prices, which is below the 0.05 R round-trip cost: the spread condition recovered +0.048 R of that loss (below the +0.08 R pre-registered threshold) but nothing more, the news-inclusive arm was no different (-0.004 vs -0.020 R, inside the 0.05 R bound: no overreaction to scheduled news either), the fill spread was 0.89 pips so cost was not the cause, and the only positive pocket (28 episodes inside the 23:50 UTC Japan-data and 06:30 BoJ windows, +0.47 R) is a post-hoc cluster of information events and is not to be chased. Do not register the follow-the-move mirror (its gross edge of about 0.02-0.04 R is less than the cost and its sign was read off this run), do not retry with M5 or H1 bars, tighter or looser spread ratios, other move sizes, limit entries (the executor pays the spread on limits too), or EURUSD and gold as the primary, and do not use the spread ratio as a filter on any other idea.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on USDJPY with 9.7 s of compute. The design did its job: the control arm was in the stage A grid, the kill arithmetic was fixed before the run after the Critic's revision, and the result is unambiguous in both directions (the hypothesis cell is flat at zero gross; the control is strongly negative on two thousand trades). This closes the last unused dimension of the price-and-quote store: clock, calendar day types, levels, move size, volume and spread have all been conditioned on and none makes an intraday USDJPY fade pay.

hypotheses.title: Japanese fiscal-calendar flows in Tokyo hours: short USDJPY in the last business days of March (and September) when exporters and institutions repatriate and square books for the fiscal year-end, long USDJPY in the first business days of April (and October) when new-year outward allocations start; each leg with a same-window ordinary-month control arm
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism: about 70 percent of listed Japanese companies close their fiscal year on 31 March (half-year on 30 September). Exporters and their overseas subsidiaries repatriate foreign-currency earnings to book them and fund year-end dividends and tax; corporate treasuries and banks square foreign-currency exposures for the balance-sheet date; life insurers, pension funds and the GPIF rebalance to fiscal-year targets. These participants must trade by a date, they execute in Tokyo hours (the Tokyo cash session and the 09:55 JST fix), and the flow is one-way (sell USD, buy JPY) and concentrated in the last two weeks of March. After 1 April the sign reverses: life insurers and pension funds deploy new-fiscal-year foreign-asset allocations, and Toshin launches cluster in April (the dealer convention of April yen selling). The other side is dealers and speculators who know the convention; the gotobi edge (post-fix short +0.14 R design, +0.11 R check, gj-strat) shows that known, dated, obligated Tokyo-hour flows still move price in this data set, and the gotobi month-end-only variant (94 trades, design +0.176 R, check +0.393 R, gotobi_tweaks) shows month-end Tokyo flows are larger than ordinary gotobi flows. This hypothesis asks whether fiscal month-ends carry a flow beyond the ordinary month-end and month-start, which the control arm measures directly. Why this is new: the flow atlas conditioned on clock x weekday, gotobi, k-th-last weekday and holiday-adjacent day types but never on the month of the year, so the fiscal calendar is the one calendar dimension the 600,912-test scan did not cover; the month-end hedge (Melvin-Prins) is an equity-hedge flow at the London 4pm fix on every month-end and is dead after 2018; the Tokyo-fix tests traded a fix minute, not the session; the gold autumn seasonal tested a diffuse festival demand with no settlement date and died, and its lesson is scoped to gold. This is a dealer convention, not a published anomaly, so it is an out-of-sample test of the convention. Design: M15 bars on USDJPY (0.6 pip median spread; about 0.7-0.9 pips at the Tokyo open), market entry at 00:00 UTC (09:00 JST, Tokyo cash open), time exit at 06:00 UTC (15:00 JST, cash close), stop 0.25 or 0.5 x ATR20, no target; one trade per selected weekday. Two legs: ye_short (last n_days weekdays of the fiscal-end months, SHORT USDJPY) and ny_long (first n_days weekdays of the new-year months, LONG USDJPY). Three month sets: mar (March / April only), mar_sep (March+September / April+October) and ctrl (the same windows in the ordinary months 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11; June and December are excluded as quarter and calendar year-ends). Counts (design 2010-2017, from the calendar, no outcomes): ye_short mar n10 = 80 trades, mar_sep n10 = 160, ctrl n10 = 480; n5 halves these; check 2018-2023 has 60 / 120 / 360. Costs: round trip about 1.7 pips (0.6-0.9 spread, 0.7 commission, 0.4 slippage) = about 0.10 R at the 0.25 x ATR stop (about 17 pips in the design years), 0.05 R at 0.5 x ATR. Expected: if the fiscal flow moves USDJPY an extra 3-4 pips per Tokyo session beyond ordinary days, the March cell nets about +0.10 R at sl 0.25 with sd about 0.7 R, design t about 1.2-1.5 on 80 trades (lower on the mar_sep cell if September is weaker); the control should sit near zero or slightly positive (the gotobi month-end effect leaks into it on 2 of every 10 days). With these counts the stage A floor passes with only about 55-60 percent probability if the effect is real, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. Human execution: two orders a day on at most 20 days a year, placed at 09:00 JST with a time exit at 15:00 JST; trivially executable on a prop account and uncorrelated in time with the vol-box, gotobi and M-3 legs except on the 2-3 gotobi dates inside each window.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: M15, sparse; locate every time by timestamp with F.first_bar_at_or_after and never assume one bar per slot.

DATE SELECTION (calendar dates, UTC): dates = unique F.utc_dates(m) with F.weekday(d) < 5 and d >= start. month(d) = calendar month number of d (1..12).
- Month sets by p['months']: if 'mar': H_short = {3}, H_long = {4}; if 'mar_sep': H_short = {3, 9}, H_long = {4, 10}; if 'ctrl': H_short = H_long = {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11}.
- Leg p['leg'] = 'ye_short': select d with month(d) in H_short and F.kth_last_weekday(dates)[d] in {0, 1, ..., n_days - 1} (the last n_days weekdays of the month; 0 = last weekday). Side = SHORT.
- Leg p['leg'] = 'ny_long': select d with month(d) in H_long and rank(d) in {0, 1, ..., n_days - 1}, where rank(d) = np.busday_count(first calendar day of d's month, d) = the number of weekdays in the month strictly before d (0 for the first weekday of the month; default Mon-Fri weekmask, no holidays). Side = LONG.
- Japanese and other holidays are not excluded (no calendar in the engine); the flow is simply absent on those days.

ENTRY: ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, 0, 0) (entry_utc '00:00'). Skip the date if ei < 1, or ei >= m.n, or m.ts[ei] is more than max_delay_min (10) minutes after d 00:00 UTC. sig = ei - 1, so the fill is at the open of bar ei (ask for longs, bid for shorts, plus slippage). entry_short[sig] = True (ye_short) or entry_long[sig] = True (ny_long); entry_type[sig] = 0; valid_bars[sig] = 1.

STOP: ATR20 = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), atr_n = 20) mapped to bars with daily.to_bars (known at the start of the trading day). Skip the date if ATR20[ei] is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[ei] (price units, > 0). tp_dist = NaN (no target). max_bars = 0.

EXIT: xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, 6, 0) (exit_utc '06:00'). Skip the date if xi >= m.n or xi <= ei. exit_short[xi - 1] = True (ye_short) or exit_long[xi - 1] = True (ny_long), so the position closes at the open of the first bar at or after 06:00 UTC. No other exits, no filters, one trade per selected date; the executor blocks overlapping entries.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): leg (grid 'ye_short', 'ny_long'), months (grid 'mar', 'mar_sep', 'ctrl'), n_days (grid 5, 10), sl_atr (grid 0.25, 0.5); fixed entry_utc '00:00', exit_utc '06:00', max_delay_min 10, atr_n 20, start '2010-01-01'. Grid = 24 cells. The 'ctrl' cells are control arms: they run at stage A only; stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout use months in {'mar', 'mar_sep'} (16 cells), set in the spec after the review step.

REPORTING (stage A table and stage C, computed from the trades): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, month-window-clustered t (R averaged per calendar month of the entry date, then a t over those month means), mean fill spread in pips, by-year avg R; for the chosen cell the avg R and count after removing gotobi dates (F.is_gotobi) and the avg R without the best two month-windows.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on USDJPY, applied by the Director even if the pipeline reports a candidate (the automatic stage A gate ranks all 24 cells by design t and a 480-trade control cell can outrank an 80-trade hypothesis cell): the best cell with months in {mar, mar_sep} must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and month-window-clustered t >= 1 with at least 80 trades; otherwise scrap. The chosen cell is that best hypothesis cell; its leg, n_days and sl_atr fix the comparisons below. (2) Control: avg R(chosen cell) minus avg R(the ctrl cell with the same leg, n_days and sl_atr) must be >= +0.06 R in design; if the ordinary months earn as much in the same window, the effect is the generic month-end or month-start Tokyo pattern that the atlas's last-weekday and k-th-weekday day types and the gotobi month-end variant already measured, and the hypothesis dies with that lesson. (3) Gotobi separation: design avg R at the chosen cell must stay > 0 after removing gotobi dates (F.is_gotobi: 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and month-end, weekend dates moved back to Friday); if it does not, the result is the gotobi short again (measured, including its month-end-only variant) and the hypothesis is dead. (4) Regime and clustering: at least 4 of the 8 design years positive at the chosen cell, and design avg R must stay > 0 after removing the best two month-windows; a result carried by one or two Marches is scrapped as an episode, not a flow. (5) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the mean fill spread is reported; if the chosen cell is positive gross but negative net, the lesson is that the fiscal flow exists but moves USDJPY by less than about 2 pips per Tokyo session and cannot be traded from the open. (6) Replication: the repatriation is against every foreign currency, so at the chosen cell the design avg R pooled over EURJPY, AUDJPY and GBPJPY must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; a USDJPY-only result with the crosses negative is scrapped as noise. (7) Legs are separate claims with their own pre-registered sign: if only one leg passes rules 1-6 the other is scrapped with its lesson and the survivor goes forward alone; neither leg's sign is ever flipped. Honest expectation: about +0.10 R net at sl 0.25 on 80 March trades, design t 1.2-1.5, mar_sep weaker if September is a smaller flow; the stage A floor passes with only about 55-60 percent probability if the effect is real at that size, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence; the most likely failure is that the flow is spread over London hours and hedged forward rather than executed spot in Tokyo, which would show as a control-sized or zero result.

hypotheses.why_different: Every calendar test in the index conditioned on weekday, k-th-last weekday, gotobi or holiday-adjacent day types (the atlas: clock x those day types x currency strength; M-3; month-end hedge at the London fix; gotobi and its 40 tweaks including the month-end-only and run-up variants), or on a fix minute (Tokyo fix long, holiday-shifted fix). None conditioned on the month of the year, so the fiscal calendar is the one calendar dimension the 600,912-test scan left unmeasured, and this hypothesis is not a re-slice of a scanned slot: the slot (one month, one session, one direction) is fixed by the mechanism before any data is seen, so the family-wise error is the 24-cell grid, not the atlas's 600k tests, which is the same logic the programme applies to every pre-registered hypothesis. The gold autumn test was a diffuse festival demand with no settlement deadline and its lesson is scoped to gold; here the participant is obligated by a balance-sheet date, as the gotobi importers are by their settlement date, and the control arm measures the generic month-end component that the gotobi month-end variant already showed to exist, so the test isolates the fiscal excess. The ny_long leg is not a snooped flip of ye_short: it is a different month, a different participant (new-year outward investors) and its sign comes from the mechanism, registered here before any run.

direction_note: Cycle 7 scraps the liquidity-withdrawal test with a lesson that closes the liquidity-provision family: the spread-conditioned fade was exactly zero gross on 160 USDJPY episodes, and the control measured the plain one-hour intraday shock fade on USDJPY at -0.068 R (t -4.5) on 2,075 design trades and -0.073 R in check, so intraday moves continue by about 2 percent of their size on mid prices, less than the round-trip cost, and the follow mirror must not be registered. One hypothesis is registered, chosen because it is the last calendar dimension the atlas did not scan (month of the year) attached to a dated, obligated Tokyo-hour participant, the only kind of flow that has survived in this data: Japanese fiscal year-end repatriation (short USDJPY in Tokyo hours in the last business days of March and September) and new-fiscal-year outflows (long in the first business days of April and October), each with a same-window ordinary-month control, gotobi separation and a three-cross replication; 24 cells, 80-160 hypothesis trades in design, expected +0.10 R and t 1.2-1.5, stage A floor about 55-60 percent likely to pass if real. After the review step the Director must set specs/auto/jpy_fiscal_year_end_repatriation.json so that stage_a carries the full 24-cell grid (controls included) and the spec grid for stages B, C and the walk-forward holds months in {mar, mar_sep} only, as was done for the liquidity test; the Builder needs no new engine helper (first-n-weekdays rank is np.busday_count from the month start). Programme status for the user: with this registration every dimension reachable from price, quote and clock data has been conditioned on at least once (clock, weekday, k-th weekday, holiday, gotobi, fiscal month, level, move size, volume, spread, cross-asset state, carry, positioning); if this test is negative, further cycles on this data store will be re-slices and should stop. The next useful inputs are external: a scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail long/short positioning, options risk reversals and implied vol, and the FX swap basis; without them the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, which is a simulation task for the engine rather than a hypothesis for this loop.
